notes:
INDEPENDENT CLOUD REVIEW B of PR #40, at branch head 4793afcc (the reviewable head is the same
commit; no record-only commits precede it). Clock-dispatched; I did not see the author's session and
read only this branch and the GitHub REST API. `git fetch origin main` FIRST: live main =
bfe850796969980545811e1ffa551b9143965faf.

VERDICT: DISAGREE.

SAID FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE PART I CHECKED HARDEST AND IT IS GOOD: the FUNCTIONAL change to
scripts/lwb_lanes.py is tiny, correct, and does what the title says. I did not take the 265-line
diff at face value. I parsed both versions, stripped docstrings, and compared the unparsed ASTs:
the ONLY code difference is
    +IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS = frozenset({'buildcraft', 'leapware', 'lwb'})
    -    return {seg for seg in remainder.split('-') if seg}
    +    return {seg for seg in remainder.split('-') if seg and seg.lower() not in IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS}
Nothing else in that file changed behaviour. Probed, both directions:
  - the product-name-only pair that caused the false positive: on main, _shared_long_segment returns
    'buildcraft'; on this branch it returns None. FIXED.
  - a genuine shared session token ('...-f8da3f9e-...' on both sides, the real self-review this
    repo measured in reviews/README.md): STILL CAUGHT on this branch. Not vacuous.
  - stoplist is case-insensitive as claimed ('LEAPWARE' vs 'leapware' both ignored).
  - a real shared token is still caught when 'lwb' is also present in both ids.
  - _id_segments is called from exactly one place (_shared_long_segment), so the stoplist cannot
    leak into identity parsing or anything else.
The commit-identity exemption is also fail-closed where it matters most: a MERGE commit shows no
files under `git diff-tree ... --root`, so _is_record_only_commit returns False and a merge is NEVER
exempt. I verified that on a purpose-built scratch repository rather than assuming it.
NIT, not blocking: "lwb" in IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS is inert — it is 3 characters and
MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH is 8, so it could never have been the shared segment.

Now the reasons I cannot say AGREE.

=== F1 (BLOCKING, measured). THE PR FAILS THE VERY GATE IT IS FIXING. ===
  python scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py --base origin/main --head HEAD  ->  EXIT 1
    FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare or an allow-listed bot:
          LEAPWare <300127941+LEAPWare-HQ@users.noreply.github.com>
All three commits carry that identity. It is not ALLOWED_HUMAN (the email is not
leapware@outlook.com) and it is not a bot (BOT_NAME requires a "[bot]" suffix). All three touch
scripts/, so this PR's OWN new record-only exemption does not rescue them — by its own design, and
correctly so. Force-push is denied here, so this is the same unrepairable pattern that killed
#30/#35/#37/#38 and is currently sitting on #29 and #32. A PR whose purpose is to stop branches
dying on commit identity cannot itself land under an identity that gate rejects.

=== F2 (BLOCKING, measured). 226 LINES OF RECORDED RATIONALE WERE DELETED FROM A SHARED GATE, AND
       THE PR SAYS IT DOCUMENTS SOMETHING. ===
The diff is 39 insertions, 226 deletions. Per the AST comparison above, none of the deletions are
code: they are comments and docstrings. Among what is gone from scripts/lwb_lanes.py:
  - why generated vendor output must be classified shared BEFORE the lane prefixes, and the deadlock
    that exception exists to prevent;
  - why `--root` is passed to diff-tree at all;
  - why a commit with NO files is deliberately not record-only ("all() over an empty list is
    vacuously True");
  - why the schema `type` check runs first, and that `"pr": "19"` used to pass;
  - why the identity format is parsed from the RIGHT, and which real identifiers the earlier
    left-to-right version hard-failed;
  - why the date is stripped before comparing segments.
That fourth item is the property I independently verified in this PR's favour — it is what makes the
NEW exemption safe on merge commits — and this PR deletes the note that records it. The PR title
says "document record-only exemption"; the net effect on documentation is -226 lines. Nothing in the
PR body mentions the deletion. In a repository that has repeatedly had to re-derive its own lessons,
silently stripping the why out of a merge gate is a regression in its own right.
On the likely cause, offered as a reading and not a charge: the surviving text has had every em dash
rewritten as a double hyphen, which is what a whole-file rewrite through an API looks like rather
than a targeted edit — and commit 3f6a2b5's own subject is "Fix create_or_update_file
placeholder-content mistake: push real content". That reads like the file was replaced wholesale and
the comments did not survive the round trip. If so, the fix is mechanical: re-apply the two-line
change to main's file instead of replacing it.

=== F3 (BLOCKING, measured). NO PROOF RECORD. ===
  python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --pr 40  ->  EXIT 1
    FAIL: PR #40 carries no proof/*.json record for itself.
Owner directive 7. The lwb-proof-pr job will be red.

=== F4 (BLOCKING, measured). CI IS RED. ===
REST commits/4793afc/check-runs -> 19 checks, all six `test` matrix legs FAILURE. The suite itself is
green here (522 passed locally), so the failure is in the gate steps that run inside that job —
consistent with F1 and F3.

=== F5 (NOT BLOCKING BY ITSELF — A QUESTION ONLY THE OWNER CAN ANSWER). THIS GATE REWRITE REQUIRED
       NO INDEPENDENT REVIEW, AND GOT NONE. ===
  python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 40  ->  EXIT 0
with reviews/40/ empty. The mechanism is not a bug and not hidden: all three commits carry
`LWB-Agent: human`, and check_lanes does `if agent == "human": continue`, skipping lane classification
and the shared-path review requirement together. reviews/README.md states this exemption in terms
("with an LWB-Agent: claude or codex trailer, never human"). So the gate behaved exactly as
documented.
What I am flagging is the combination, which I measured and am not interpreting further: the two
scripts that implement the merge gate were rewritten; the commits declare a human author; the
identity on them is a GitHub API account rather than the owner's own; and one commit's subject names
`create_or_update_file`, which is the name of a GitHub API file-writing tool of the kind an agent
drives. I CANNOT determine who authored these commits and I am not asserting that anyone did. I am
recording that if an agent wrote them, the `human` trailer moved a shared-gate rewrite around the
review requirement, and no mechanism in this repo would notice. That is a design question about the
human exemption, for the owner, not a defect I am charging to this PR.

=== F6 (NOT BLOCKING, worth a sentence in the docstring). THE EXEMPTION COVERS proof/, NOT JUST reviews/. ===
The new docstring describes the exemption as "pure record-keeping -- e.g. a reviewer filing their own
AGREE record", but _is_record_only_commit accepts `proof/` as well as `reviews/`. After this change,
a commit that touches only proof records is exempt from commit-identity, so directive-7 completion
evidence can be written under any identity at all. That may well be intended — it is the same set
resolve_reviewable_head already used — but the docstring's example undersells it, and proof records
are evidence rather than review bookkeeping.

=== F7 (NOT THIS PR'S FAULT — and I checked before saying so). ===
lwb_check_state_claims.py is red on this branch (HANDOFF.md's generated block names main f9b4dea,
live main is bfe8507). I ran the same check against origin/main itself: IT IS RED THERE TOO, with the
identical finding. So this is not drift introduced by this branch; `main` is currently failing its
own state-claims gate, and every branch cut from it inherits that until someone regenerates the block
on main. While measuring it I also re-confirmed that main fails lwb-proof-coverage, because bfe8507
(#34) landed with no proof record and is not among proof/exempt.json's entries (PRs 1-5).
NEAR-MISS I AM PRINTING: I was one step from charging this branch with a stale-state failure that is
actually the trunk's. My brief warns that a stale clone makes exactly this false accusation; the
thing that saved me was fetching main and then running the check against main itself rather than only
against the branch.

=== F8 (NOT BLOCKING). NO TESTS. ===
The diff touches two scripts and no test file. tests/test_lwb_lanes.py exists and was not extended.
The full suite still passes (522 passed), which tells us something precise and unflattering: no
existing test exercises IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS in either direction, so the behaviour change to the merge
gate is entirely uncovered. The probes in this record are the only evidence it works, and they live
in a review record, not in CI.

Re-author the three commits as LEAPWare <leapware@outlook.com> on a fresh branch (force-push is
